title: Hosted API latency bands and backpressure gating policy for bursty workloads
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem summary:
Hosted text-generation endpoints experience periodic high-concurrency bursts (traffic spikes from client-side fanout) that cause long-tail latency spikes and elevated token costs. Current rollout gates are largely static (canary percentage + basic SLO checks) and don't account for transient request storms or per-tenant burst behavior. We need a product-level definition and acceptance criteria for: 1) latency Availability/Latency SLO bands broken down by percentile and sequence-length buckets, 2) error-budget driven progressive throttling/backpressure policies (per-tenant and global), 3) failover/degradation rules (downgrade model variant, reduce max tokens, or switch to non-streaming mode), and 4) rollout gating rules that tie canary traffic weight to running error budget and backpressure alarms.
Goals:
- Define explicit, testable SLOs for P50/P90/P95/P99 across three payload classes (short: <128 tokens, medium: 128–1024, long: >1024) for hosted text-generation endpoints.
- Specify error budget burn rate thresholds that trigger staged actions (e.g., 10% burn in 1h = alert; 30% = pause rollout; 70% = emergency rollback to previous model).
- Design per-tenant and global backpressure policy: queuing limits, token-rate throttles, and adaptive shed rules to protect core customers.
- Produce rollout gate matrix that maps canary weight, observed latency bands, and error-budget state to allowed next-step actions (increase, hold, rollback), and automated enforcement mechanism in the control plane.
Non-goals: deep kernel/runtime scheduling changes (eng will own implementation), pricing changes, or account-level quota redesign (separate initiative).
Deliverables:
- PRD for SLO definitions and gating matrix (this ticket)).
- API contract for publishing backpressure signals to customer-facing metrics (Console and usage API).
- Acceptance test plan and load jobs for CI that simulate bursty fanout and validate automated gates.
- Rollout playbook for on-call, including incident runbooks and rollback thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: SLO table published with explicit percentiles and payload buckets and signed off by runtime and infra leads
Error-budget policy doc with numeric thresholds and automated actions (alerting, hold, rollback) included in the PRD
Backpressure policy defined with per-tenant token-rate limits, global queue depth thresholds, and degradation ladder (model-switch, token_limit, non-stream fallback)
Control plane gating matrix created and implemented in a feature-flagged path for canary deploys
CI load tests reproduce a synthetic burst and exercise the gating matrix; green on canary hold/rollback scenarios
Console surfaces new SLO metrics and error-budget burn rate; engineering dashboard shows backpressure events and tenant-level throttling logs
Runbook for on-call with clear escalation steps, owner, and post-incident action items attached
